What common student misconceptions or gaps in knowledge were seen in the responses to this
question?
Common Misconceptions/Knowledge Gaps Responses that Demonstrate Understanding
• In part (a) many responses used a global argument,
claiming that “ ( ) 0 f x ′ > to the left of 6 and
( ) 0 f x ′ > to the right of 6.” This statement implies
that ( ) f x ′ is always non-negative, which is not true.
• Some responses used a precalculus argument that “ f
doesn’t change from increasing to decreasing or vice
versa,” without reference to the behavior of . f ′
• Many responses used vague language such as “the
function doesn’t change signs” or “it doesn’t change
signs.”
• ( ) f x ′ does not change sign at 6. x =
• Because ( ) f x ′ does not change sign at 6, x = the
function f has neither a local maximum nor a local
minimum at this point.
• In part (b) many responses reasoned that f is concave
down on the presented intervals because ( ) 0 f x ′′ <
there, without tying the argument to the given graph of
. f ′
• Some responses reported the interval ( ) 1, 2 , − where the
graph of f ′ is negative.
• Some responses made an argument based on the
concavity of the given graph of f ′ and, therefore,
concluded there were no intervals where the graph of f
is concave down.
• The graph of f is concave down on ( ) 2, 0 − and
( ) 4, 6 , because slope of f f ′′ ′ = is negative on these
intervals.
• The graph of f is concave down on ( ) 2, 0 − and
( ) 4, 6 , because f ′ is decreasing on these intervals.
• In part (c) the most common mistake was to use
L’Hospital’s Rule without first checking that the limits
of the numerator and of the denominator were both 0.
